commits.subject: Retract my own port-cost overestimate WHERE IT LIVES: 59 closure modules was an import count, not a dependency count
commits.summary:
**Docstring only, code byte-identical, rebuilt (8581 jobs, exit 0).** Three sites in this file were stale the moment FiberVanishing/FiberBound landed. (1) The antecedent is no longer unwitnessed: the paragraph saying AJC proves it at no proper curve is now marked HISTORY and points at exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_curve, which carries three curve binders and no vanishing hypothesis. (2) "until it lands, every star fires only under a hypothesis AJC cannot supply" -- it landed. (3) The genus-zero specialisation no longer needs to send readers to an unported theorem.

**The retraction that is worth more than the fix.** This file priced the port at 59 closure modules with an unavoidable Picard-presentation dependency, "~2.5k lines and a Picard dependency", and told the reader not to re-guess it. That number counted IMPORT LINES. By DECLARATION REFERENCE the vanishing chain uses picClass, CechPic, divisorClass and classDeg zero times; the twelve Picard modules hung off class-side material the argument never mentions, and the single edge that carried anything real was carrying the coeffAt calculus. Corrected in place, with the general lesson stated: an import closure is an upper bound and can overstate tenfold when a file bundles a construction with its class theory.
